description: Six trigger sequencers of up to 32 steps, each with sixteen patterns and five level knobs a step can draw its CV from

params.text: Sets the voltage that row's CV output takes on a step drawn at the lowest of the five levels
Sets the voltage that row's CV output takes on a step drawn at the second of the five levels
Sets the voltage that row's CV output takes on a step drawn at the middle of the five levels
Sets the voltage that row's CV output takes on a step drawn at the fourth of the five levels
Sets the voltage that row's CV output takes on a step drawn at the highest of the five levels

inputs.text: A rising edge here returns every row to its first step
A rising edge here queues the next pattern on all six rows
A rising edge here advances that row one step; with nothing patched, the row follows the clock of the first row
A rising edge here queues the next pattern for that row, which takes effect when the row reaches its first step
Held above 0V this silences every trigger output and freezes every CV output at its last value

outputs.text: A 1ms 10V pulse on each step the pattern marks
The level of the current step scaled to the full range set on the menu, or a bipolar version of it when the Bi-Dir switch for that row is on
A 1ms 10V pulse each time that row returns to its first step

notes: a row plays nothing until a clock is patched to its CLK input, or to the CLK input of the first row, which the other five follow when their own is empty
every step of a new module is off, so clicking steps into the grid is what makes a row produce anything
left-clicking a step in the grid raises it one level, cycling through the five levels and back to off, and right-clicking a step turns it off
the row of marks above a row's steps sets the last step in the run
the upper row of marks above the Pat strip sets the last pattern in the run, and the lower row picks which pattern is shown
menu: VRange (15, 10, 5): — sets the full scale of every CV output, and each click on the item steps it from 15V to 10V to 5V and round again; the setting in force is printed beside the item
